name: Brassica juncea
description: A leafy mustard grown for its peppery leaves, which are eaten raw or cooked. It does best in rich, consistently moist soil.
care_note: It self-seeds and can become weedy.

name: Eruca vesicaria
description: A fast cool-season salad green with peppery leaves. Its flowers and young seed pods are edible too.
edible: leaves, flowers, young seed pods and seeds

name: Spinacia oleracea
description: A cool-season leafy green for salads and cooking. It tolerates more shade than most vegetables and grows well in containers.

name: Allium tuberosum
description: A clumping perennial herb with garlic-flavoured leaves and small cream flowers in summer. It self-seeds and spreads underground, so many people grow it in a pot.

name: Asparagus officinalis
description: A long-lived perennial vegetable grown for its young spears, which are picked in early spring.

toxic.note: The berries can upset the stomach if eaten, and handling raw young shoots can irritate skin. Please keep children from eating the berries.

name: Cynara cardunculus
description: A large, thistle-like perennial grown as globe artichoke and cardoon. Its purple flowers in summer and autumn attract bees and butterflies, and the blanched leaf stalks and the roots are cooked as vegetables.
care_note: It can spread from gardens and become an invasive weed.

name: Apium graveolens
description: A biennial vegetable grown for its crisp leaf stalks. Its umbrella-like heads of small white flowers attract bees and butterflies.

name: Pastinaca sativa
description: A biennial cool-season root vegetable whose sweet taproot is eaten in its first year, raw or cooked.

toxic.note: The sap makes skin sensitive to sunlight and can cause burns and blisters. Please wear gloves and long sleeves when handling the leaves and stems.

name: Solanum tuberosum
description: A perennial from South America grown as an annual crop for its tubers.

toxic.note: The leaves, stems, sprouts and any green parts of the tubers contain solanine, which can be fatal. Please discard sprouts and tubers that are green under the skin, and keep children and pets from eating the plant.

name: Cucumis melo
description: A warm-season annual vine grown for sweet melons such as cantaloupes and honeydews. Bees pollinate its yellow flowers.

name: Citrullus lanatus
description: A sprawling annual vine with large, juicy fruit. It does best where summers are long and warm, planted after the last frost.

name: Cucurbita moschata
description: A vigorous warm-season vine that trails along the ground or climbs with tendrils, grown for butternut and other winter squash. It prefers moderately moist soil.

name: Abelmoschus esculentus
description: A warm-season vegetable that grows into a branched plant about a metre tall, with yellow flowers and edible pods. Plant it after the last frost.

toxic.note: The plant can irritate skin. Please wear gloves when picking.

name: Hibiscus sabdariffa
description: A woody subshrub related to okra. Its calyces and flowers flavour and colour teas, and its leaves are cooked like a spicy spinach.

name: Vicia faba
description: A self-fertile annual legume grown for its nutritious seeds and pods. It fixes nitrogen from the air, so it is often grown as a cover crop.

toxic.note: People with the inherited condition favism can develop a serious blood disorder after eating the beans. Please check with a doctor if favism runs in the family.

name: Phaseolus coccineus
description: A climbing bean that can reach 3 or 4 metres, with red, orange or white flowers in summer and autumn and edible pods.

toxic.note: Raw or undercooked beans can cause severe nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea. Please cook the beans thoroughly.

name: Vigna unguiculata
description: A tropical annual climber grown for its long, slender beans, picked while young. It copes with heat, humidity, drought and poor soil.

name: Colocasia esculenta
description: A tender, clumping perennial with very large leaves that grows from a corm. The corm is a staple food in the tropics, but every part is poisonous until thoroughly cooked.
edible: corms and leaves, only after thorough cooking

toxic.note: Eaten raw, every part makes the mouth, tongue and lips swell painfully. Please cook it thoroughly, and keep children from chewing the leaves.

name: Zingiber officinale
description: The true ginger, a tropical perennial from Asia grown for its pungent, aromatic rhizomes. In cooler areas it can be grown in a pot.

name: Curcuma longa
description: An upright perennial herb about a metre tall whose bright yellow-orange rhizomes are boiled, dried and ground into the spice turmeric.

toxic.note: The rhizomes can irritate skin. Please wear gloves when handling them.

name: Cichorium endivia
description: A bitter salad green that forms a loose rosette of curly or broad leaves. Its blue flowers are edible too.

name: Helianthus tuberosus
description: A tall perennial sunflower grown for its edible tubers, with yellow flowers late in summer and into autumn.
care_note: It can become weedy, so please plant it where it can be contained.

name: Lagenaria siceraria
description: An annual climbing vine with large white flowers that open at night, grown for its oddly shaped gourds.
edible: young fruit, leaves, flowers and young stems
care_note: Hand pollination helps the fruit set.

name: Momordica charantia
description: A vigorous, frost-tender annual vine that grows 4 to 6 metres in a season, with yellow flowers and bitter fruit that is eaten young as a vegetable.

toxic.note: Ripe fruit, rinds and seeds are toxic in large amounts. Please eat only young fruit.

name: Salvia officinalis
description: A short-lived, bushy, aromatic herb whose leaves season meat, vegetables, eggs and stuffing. Bees and butterflies visit its summer flowers.

name: Origanum majorana
description: A small, aromatic perennial herb from the Mediterranean with a sweet, spicy flavour, best picked before its small white flowers open in summer.

toxic.note: It can upset the stomach of cats and dogs. Please keep pets from eating it.

name: Melissa officinalis
description: A bushy, lemon-scented perennial herb whose leaves and flowers make tea and flavour soups and stews.

name: Mentha × piperita
description: A cross of watermint and spearmint grown for its leaves. It spreads by rhizomes into an aggressive groundcover.

name: Anethum graveolens
description: An aromatic, self-seeding annual herb with heads of yellow flowers in summer that bees and butterflies visit.

name: Matricaria chamomilla
description: An annual herb with fragrant, finely divided leaves and small white daisies with yellow centres in summer and autumn. The flowers are dried for tea.

toxic.note: People allergic to daisies can react with a rash, hives or swelling, and it can upset the stomach of cats and dogs. Please stop using it if it causes a reaction, and keep pets from eating it.

name: Chamaemelum nobile
description: A low, creeping perennial chamomile with white daisies from spring to autumn. It copes with drought, poor soil and foot traffic.

toxic.note: It can cause skin rashes and allergic reactions in sensitive people, and vomiting and diarrhoea in cats and dogs. Please wear gloves if your skin reacts, and keep pets from eating it.

name: Artemisia dracunculus
description: A perennial herb grown for its aromatic leaves. Culinary tarragon was selected from this wild species, which likes dry, well-drained soil.

toxic.note: Eating it can cause vomiting, drooling and diarrhoea in dogs and cats, and the sap can irritate skin. Please keep pets from eating it, and wear gloves if your skin reacts.

name: Laurus nobilis
description: An evergreen tree or shrub from the Mediterranean whose leaves are used to flavour food.

toxic.note: Eating the leaves can cause vomiting and diarrhoea in cats and dogs. Please keep pets from chewing them.

name: Stevia rebaudiana
description: A tender perennial from Brazil and Paraguay grown for its very sweet leaves, which are eaten fresh or dried and ground as a sugar substitute.

name: Symphytum officinale
description: A vigorous perennial with large leaves and bell-shaped pink, purple or white flowers in spring and summer that bees visit. It was long used as a medicinal herb.

toxic.note: Eating it can cause liver and lung damage and cancer. Please do not eat it or drink it as tea.

care_note: It spreads and can become weedy.

name: Plectranthus amboinicus
description: A fleshy perennial herb with a strong scent of oregano when crushed. It grows mostly in spring and summer and likes a hot, dry spot.

name: Ocimum tenuiflorum
description: An aromatic annual or short-lived perennial basil from southern Asia, cooked like sweet basil, with a flavour of clove, mint and basil.
care_note: It self-seeds and can become weedy.

name: Thymus × citriodorus
description: A low, mounding evergreen subshrub with lemon-scented leaves and pink flowers in summer that bees and butterflies visit.

name: Levisticum officinale
description: A tall perennial culinary herb with fragrant leaves. Every part can be eaten: the seeds in breads and cakes, and the leaves in tea, soups and stews.

name: Capsicum chinense
description: A chilli species from South America that includes the habanero and some of the hottest chillies grown, such as 'Carolina Reaper'. It needs rich, moist, well-drained soil and full sun.

toxic.note: The fruit is extremely hot. Please keep it away from children, and wash your hands after handling it.

name: Mentha australis
description: A sprawling native mint from creek banks with fresh, minty leaves for tea, salads and sauces. It suckers through beds, so a pot or a root barrier keeps it in place.
pruning: It can get leggy and responds well to pruning.

name: Apium prostratum
description: A low coastal herb that can stay compact like parsley or cascade over banks and pots. Its leaves are used like parsley or celery, and it self-seeds readily.
care_note: It grows best in part shade and needs extra care in full sun.

name: Atriplex nummularia
description: A sprawling, silver-leaved shrub from the arid inland. It tolerates high salinity, alkaline soil and severe drought, and its leaves and seeds are eaten fresh or dried.
care_note: It will not tolerate waterlogging or high humidity.
